## What I changed

Only `settings.py` was edited (no new workspace files):

```python
"""Read line-based application settings."""

def parse_settings(text):
    settings = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        name, _, value = line.partition("=")
        settings[name.strip()] = value.strip()
    return settings
```

## Why

The original one-liner `dict(line.split("=") for line in text.splitlines())` had three bugs:

1. **Blank/whitespace-only lines** — `"".split("=")` yields `[""]`, so `dict(...)` raised `ValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required`. This is exactly the failure `public_checks.py` reproduces with `"name=demo\n\n"`.
2. **`=` inside a value** — `split("=")` produced more than two parts, again raising `ValueError`. Using `partition("=")` splits only at the **first** `=`, so `url=http://x/?a=b=c` keeps the full value.
3. **Untrimmed names/values** — `"b = 2 "` previously gave key `"b "` and value `" 2 "`. Now both sides are `.strip()`ed.

Empty input (`""` or whitespace-only) returns `{}` because every line is skipped.

## Verification

- `python -B public_checks.py` → passes.
- Extra assertions (empty input, whitespace-only input, padded keys/values, multiple `=` in a value, empty value) all pass.
